description:
## Problem
`src/vug/fetcher.cr:147-159` (`handle_result_action`) has a `case` over the `Action` enum with an explicit `else` branch and a comment "ReturnResult / UseCached are handled by the caller":

```crystal
case action
when .redirect?
  ...
when .try_fallback?
  ...
else
  # ReturnResult / UseCached are handled by the caller
end
```

This `else` is dead — the only caller (`apply_action`) already filters on `action.redirect? || action.try_fallback?` before calling. The `else` masks the fact that the case is exhaustive for the intended inputs and prevents Crystal's exhaustiveness check from warning if a new enum value is added.

## Fix
Remove the `else` branch. If Crystal warns about non-exhaustive `case` on the enum, let the warning surface (it's the intended safety net) and either:
- Add explicit `when .return_result?, .use_cached?` no-op cases with a brief comment, or
- Convert to `case ... in ... end` pattern matching that fails loudly on unhandled variants.

## Why
- Readability: code reflects the actual control contract.
- Safety: future enum additions cause compile-time feedback.

## Acceptance
- [ ] `else` branch removed (or replaced with explicit no-op cases for `ReturnResult` and `UseCached`).
- [ ] All existing tests pass.
- [ ] `ameba src/` reports 0 failures.
- [ ] Public API unchanged.

## Out of scope
- Do not change `Action` enum values.
- Do not refactor `apply_action` (covered by a separate ticket).
title: fetcher: remove dead else branch in handle_result_action
